Section 6 • \(P\)3D with the discrete Fourier transform

6.1 Configuration-space and Fourier-space grids

We take a square transverse domain of side \(L_\perp\) (\(|\mathcal{A}_\perp|=L_\perp^2\)) with \(N_\perp\times N_\perp\) sightlines on a regular grid, and \(N_\Lambda\) pixels along each sightline: \begin{align} &\vec{x}_{\perp}[\vec{n}]=d_\perp\,\vec{n}, \qquad \Lambda[m]=\Lambda_a+m\,d\Lambda, \qquad d_\perp\equiv\frac{L_\perp}{N_\perp}, \qquad d\Lambda\equiv\frac{L_\Lambda}{N_\Lambda}, \notag\\ &\vec{n}\in\{0,\dots,N_\perp-1\}^2, \qquad m\in\{0,\dots,N_\Lambda-1\}, \tag{6.1} \end{align} with \(\delta_i^{(s)}[\vec{n},m]\equiv\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp[\vec{n}],\Lambda[m])\). We denote by \(V\equiv L_\perp^2L_\Lambda\) the volume, \(N\equiv N_\perp^2N_\Lambda\) the number of cells, and \(v\equiv V/N=d_\perp^2\,d\Lambda\) the cell volume. The DFT is defined only at the discrete modes \begin{equation} \vec{k}_\perp[\vec{p}]=\frac{2\pi}{L_\perp}\,\vec{p}, \qquad k_\parallel[q]=\frac{2\pi}{L_\Lambda}\,q, \qquad \vec{p}\in\left\{-\tfrac{N_\perp}{2},\dots,\tfrac{N_\perp}{2}-1\right\}^2, \quad q\in\left\{-\tfrac{N_\Lambda}{2},\dots,\tfrac{N_\Lambda}{2}-1\right\}, \tag{6.2} \end{equation} spaced by the fundamental modes \(k_{\rm f,\perp}\equiv2\pi/L_\perp\), \(k_{\rm f,\parallel}\equiv2\pi/L_\Lambda\) and bounded by the Nyquist wavenumbers \(k_{\rm Ny,\perp}\equiv\pi/d_\perp\), \(k_{\rm Ny,\parallel}\equiv\pi/d\Lambda\): the finite size of the domain discretizes Fourier space, and the finite resolution bounds it (Fig. 12).
